claims.text: Adding 30% AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder to ZrB2 and SPS-consolidating it at 1500 °C will improve densification and grain bonding.
The resulting cermet will have superior mechanical properties to single-phase ZrB2 and specimens sintered at lower or higher temperatures.
The resulting cermet will have greater high-temperature oxidation resistance than single-phase ZrB2 and specimens sintered at lower or higher temperatures.
The resulting cermet will have greater molten-aluminum corrosion resistance than single-phase ZrB2 and specimens sintered at lower or higher temperatures.
At 1500 °C, the AlFeNiCoCr binder becomes sufficiently fluid to infiltrate the ZrB2 matrix uniformly.
The binder fills pores and bonds ZrB2 grains during SPS at 1500 °C.
Binder overflow occurs when the cermet is sintered at 1600 °C.
Sintering at 1500 °C produces a relative density of approximately 97.7%.
Binder-assisted pore filling and grain bonding create a compact microstructure.
Increased densification reduces pathways for molten-aluminum ingress.
Improved grain bonding minimizes grain-boundary cracking or detachment.
Reduced porosity and improved grain bonding increase hardness and fracture toughness.
Reduced porosity and improved grain bonding increase molten-aluminum corrosion and wear resistance.
Among cermets sintered at 1300, 1400, 1500, and 1600 °C, the 1500 °C specimen will have the highest relative density.
The 1500 °C specimen will have greater hardness and fracture toughness than the other sintering-temperature conditions.
The fracture toughness of the 1500 °C cermet will exceed the approximately 4.5 MPa·m^1/2 toughness attributed to pure ZrB2.
The 1500 °C specimen will have lower molten-aluminum corrosion rates than specimens sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
The 1500 °C specimen will have lower wear volume than specimens sintered at 1300, 1400, or 1600 °C.
